articles.title: Pokemon: Diamond and Pearl Box Set 1 - IGN
articles.summary: This is not going to go down in history as a leap forward in animation. Honestly, for all it's a decent kids' show, it's not even at the point where adults are going to be able to watch it for more than a couple of minutes without getting restless. In 20-odd years, though, when the kids of today start feeling '00s nostalgia and make the mistake of trying to enjoy the cartoons of their youth, they probably won't feel quite as bad as we do when we realize how awful M.A.S.K. was.
articles.body:
If you grew up in the '80s, like a lot of you probably did, the DVD era may have had some unintended consequences for you. A lot of the TV cartoons we loved as children are out on DVD now, and if you buy those DVDs and watch them today, you know what you'll find out? Those shows were bad .

Seriously. Horrible. They looked like hacked-out crap and they were terribly written even if you take into account the fact that they were designed for the sole purpose of selling toys to six-year-olds. Transformers nostalgia runs rampant around the internet, but you might notice that it tends to focus on the toys more than the show. That's because the Transformers show was godawful, and Transformers was one of the good ones, the ones with a budget and some talent behind them. Pick up the Galaxy High School box set and see how many episodes you can sit through before you pass out and choke to death on your own vomit.

What does this have to do with Pokemon ? Well, it helps to give a show like this a little historical perspective. On a mechanical level, Pokemon today is what Jayce and the Wheeled Warriors was 20-some years ago (just to pull an example out of a hat). It's the advertising/entertainment arm of a multi-pronged marketing enterprise – another toy commercial, although the toys are a lot more complicated than they used to be. It may not be great entertainment, especially if you're more than six years old, but it does its job better than, say, Rubik the Amazing Cube did.

These two discs feature the first 17 episodes of Diamond and Pearl , the latest evolution of the series, based on the new Nintendo DS videogame. Brock and Ash are back, but Misty is gone. She's been replaced by Dawn, a fresh face dedicated to succeeding her mother as a Pokemon Coordinator. "Coordinating" Pokemon goes one step beyond simply training them – Dawn's ultimate ambition seems to involve winning the Pokemon equivalent of the Miss America competition, but if I'm wrong I'm sure some six-year-old will rapidly be able to correct me.

Despite those kinds of superficial changes, Pokemon is still more or less the same show on a mechanical level. Our heroes wander around the world, join competitions, encounter rivals (more than a decade after their debut, Team Rocket are still our heroes' perennial opponents), and admire lots of different kinds of cute monster antics. The addition of all the new Diamond and Pearl monsters (on top of the Gold and Silver monsters and the now-old-school original 100 from Red and Blue) gives the show a gigantic array of Pokemon to pick from, and the old favorites haven't been sacrificed just to give the new monsters extra promotion.

That's the real draw of the series, of course. The people involved aren't very interesting – they're just more cartoon humans, and they act like one-note cartoon humans have since the dawn of color television. (Not to mention, the "best by" date on James' raving queen act sailed past us maybe five or six years ago.)

The monsters, on the other hand, are the unpredictable part, and the show makes the most of them. Digital animation nowadays lets you produce a good-looking TV show on a shoestring. The visual style of Pokemon hasn't changed a whole lot, but Diamond and Pearl has a much sharper picture and much smoother animation, which does a lot for the newer, more detailed monster designs.

"Pokemon" is the name on the marquee, and that aspect of the series is still a lot of fun. The better episodes on these discs come up with more for them to do then just fight with each other, while the weaker ones still make the most of the monsters' innate visual charm. When you think about it, the best of all possible Pokemon TV shows might be one without any humans in it at all. At the very least, it would save on the cost of voice actors

The 17 episodes included on this box set are split up on only two discs, but given that they're dual-layer discs, there's only one voice track, and the episodes are presented in an ordinary 4:3 TV aspect ratio, there are enough bits to go around and keep the show looking good. The picture is sharp and all the day-glo kids'-show colors are bright and inviting without seeming too garish or weird. (Well, they might seem garish or weird if you're over the age of 30, but in that case we can't help you.)

As mentioned above, there's only one voice track here, with the Viz-produced English dub. This is not a show that will demand any extra effort from your sound system, but the dub is surprisingly good. The actors behind most of these characters have been voicing them for years now – Addie Blaustein is great at delivering Meowth's snarky dialogue -- and the script actually features a smoother rewrite job than some shows that are supposed to be aimed at a more mature audience.

While most anime publishers are slimming down their packages as much as possible these days, the Diamond and Pearl sets are sticking with an old-fashioned format. Each disc comes in its own plastic keepcase (with monster profiles on the back covers, besides just the episode listing), and the two fit into a cardboard slipcase.

On the discs themselves, there's nothing extra to speak of at all. This still isn't that bad a deal, though – the suggested retail price for this set is only $25, and you can get it at a discount all over the place.

This is not going to go down in history as a leap forward in animation. Honestly, for all it's a decent kids' show, it's not even at the point where adults are going to be able to watch it for more than a couple of minutes without getting restless. In 20-odd years, though, when the kids of today start feeling '00s nostalgia and make the mistake of trying to enjoy the cartoons of their youth, they probably won't feel quite as bad as we do when we realize how awful M.A.S.K. was.

articles.title: The 7 Best Jigsaw Puzzle Brands Based on Quality and Price
articles.summary: From Ravensburger to Springbok to Rokr, here are the best puzzle brands to check out in 2026.
articles.body:
Piecing together a puzzle is a great way to relax. Whether you enjoy the hobby on your own or with others, there's quite a few different formats to choose from these days, too. There are some types of puzzles that offer fun 3D builds that bring your efforts to life and some even tell a story with a secret ending that ties it all together. If you don't frequently build puzzles, though, finding a good option like the ones previously mentioned means tracking down a reliable brand first and going from there.

One visit to Amazon will show you that there's an abundance of companies offering different puzzles at varying price points, which can feel quite overwhelming. We're here to help, though. In this list, we've gathered up some of our favorite puzzle brands that we believe are worth dropping money on and noted some puzzles from each that we highly recommend. If you've been itching to pick up something new to get stuck into, have a look at our collection of the best puzzle brands below.

Ravensburger is a brand that's been around for a while, offering a wide range of puzzle sizes from smaller 500-piece options - and even lower, if you prefer - to one of the largest puzzles with 40,000 pieces . Yes, really! The puzzle pieces are cut to fit neatly into place, with the company stating on its website that its "puzzles are made using custom-built tools and steel strips, handcrafted by skilled artisans. This meticulous process ensures each piece fits perfectly, providing a flawless puzzle experience without any false fits." The company also notes that each puzzle goes through quality checks, so you know you're getting a product that'll last. It's also worth noting that Ravensburger puzzles are even used in the world jigsaw puzzle championship .

Below you can find some Ravensburger puzzles we'd recommend in a wide range of sizes. Starting from just 500 pieces and going up to a whopping 5,000, there's a puzzle for every challenge level available. We've even included a couple of their 3D puzzles if you want a finished product that you can set up afterward. Ravensburger also has many officially licensed puzzles from franchises like Harry Potter , Star Wars , and The Lord of the Rings .

Ravensburger Tropical Waters 500-Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Ravensburger Myths & Legends 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Ravensburger Dean Macadam Most Everyone is Mad

Ravensburger Disney-Pixar Toy Store Jigsaw Puzzle - 1000 Pieces

Ravensburger Pokemon Pokeball 3D Jigsaw Puzzle Ball - 54 Pieces

Ravensburger Midnight at The Library 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Ravensburger Universal Amblin Jigsaw Puzzle - 2000 Pieces

Ravensburger Reign of Dragons 3000-Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Ravensburger Solar System 540-Piece - 9 Planet 3D Jigsaw Puzzle Set

Ravensburger Pokemon 5000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

The Magic Puzzle Company really lives up to its name. Its magical puzzles combine a "traditional jigsaw puzzle experience with ideas from the worlds of tabletop games and magic," according to its website . It's become a very beloved brand as well, with its Kickstarter boasting 62,284 backers from when it was last updated. Each of its 1,000-piece puzzles features over 50 easter eggs for you to find, but the coolest part about them is the special secret ending you get after finishing the first part of the puzzle. This important element helps tie together the story from the first set of pieces in the box, making it even more satisfying to finish. There are now a total of five full series' releases of these puzzles with the final Series Five puzzles arriving at Amazon in early 2026. The first Series Six puzzle is available as of August, with two more expected by 2027.

Each puzzle from the Magic Puzzle Company offers a unique experience with original art, to boot. We've included a few of our recommended puzzles below that each have something interesting to bring to the table, from the magical Mystic Maze to the colorful Gnomes' Homes .

Recommended Puzzles From Magic Puzzle Company

Springbok is another well-regarded brand that's been around for a very long time - since 1963 to be exact. The company offers a variety of different puzzles to choose from so you can find an option that best suits your personal tastes and skill level. Each one is made with a lot of love, too. The company prides itself on creating quality puzzles, stating on its website that, "The quality of our dies and above average thickness of our chipboards ensures the interlocking pieces will come together flawlessly multiple times."

From piecing it together to admiring the final work and all of the details within it, Springbok's puzzles will keep you busy for quite a while. Below we've included a few fun puzzles from their collections, from a selection of sweet treats to a puzzle paying homage to some excellent films.

Springbok's 500 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle Sweet Tooth, Multi

Springbok's 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle Gamer's Trove, Multi

Springbok's 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle Snack Treats

Springbok Groovy Records 1000 piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Springbok - Retro Refreshments - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Springbok - Dream Garage - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Heye's puzzles come in a fun variety of unique designs and ones with incredible amounts of detail. On its website , you can find the 'Puzzle' category broken down into five sections: Art Lab, Cartoon, Fantasy, Fine Art, and Photo Art. Each of these is further broken down into more sections so you can explore the many different styles of puzzle that are available. Not only that, but Heye also offers a range of puzzle sizes, from 500 pieces to 6,000, so you can easily find one that fits the challenge level you're looking for.

On top of its creative puzzle designs, the company also notes on its website that, "HEYE puzzles have been successively converted to plastic-free production without plastic bags and shrink wrap." That's a very big win for sustainability. Below you can find just a few of our recommended puzzles from Heye.

Heye 29787 "Flower's Life" Puzzle (1000-Piece)

Heye Garden Adventure 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Heye Polar Habitat Degano Puzzles (1000-Piece)

Heye 29777 Ocean Habitat Puzzle (1000-Piece)

Heye Triangular Fairy Tales Prades Puzzles (1500-Piece)

Heye Puzzles - 1000 Pc -Selfie (Zozoville)

Not all puzzles come in a 2D format. If you're looking for something a little different to work with, Rokr offers a great collection of 3D builds that can up your puzzling game with their intricate designs. With 10 years of experience and, according to its website , 4,190 Happy Members, Rokr is a reliable brand for those looking to expand on their puzzling skills. Its models are built to last, too. On its website , the company states that it prioritizes, "the use of durable, child-safe materials to ensure that our products not only withstand the rigors of play but also provide a reliable and secure play environment."

Below we've listed just a few of our favorite puzzles from Rokr, from an illuminated globe to a miniature pinball machine. These come with varying amounts of puzzle pieces as well, so there's a little something for every challenge level here. If you're looking for a good LEGO alternative , we recommend starting witht his brand.

ROKR 3D Wooden Puzzles Marble Run Model Building Kit

ROKR 3D Wooden Puzzles Illuminated Globe with Stand

ROKR 3D Wooden Puzzles Miniature Pinball Machine

Buffalo Games is another brand that's been in the game for a while, since 1986. The company has crafted numerous puzzles since then, with care for their construction at the forefront of its mind. According to its website , the company states that, "With a careful eye for quality and sustainability, our puzzles use the thickest graphic board, premium paper, and sturdy set-up boxes." Each puzzle is also "manufactured using a precision cutting technique that guarantees every piece snaps into place with our signature Perfect Snap™ technology."

Whether you want a puzzle with a scenic view or one that captures your favorite piece of entertainment, Buffalo Games has quite a few options to choose from. We've included just a few of our favorites below in varying sizes, from 300 to 2,000 pieces. It's also worth noting that this brand makes some of the very best Pokemon puzzles on the market for both kis and adults.

Buffalo Games - Cinque Terre - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Buffalo Games - Pokémon - Fan Favorites - 300 Large Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

Buffalo Games - Alpine Serenity - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle with Hidden Images

Buffalo Games - James Mertke - Simple Succulent - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

The New York Puzzle Company was founded in 2007, but it has grown substantially since then. It now includes licenses from quite a few popular franchises including Harry Potter, Peter Rabbit, and The New Yorker. According to the company's about us page , these puzzle makers try to focus on picking evocative images and providing the right level of challenge. You can really see that idealogy in every puzzle, and each and every one is fit to be framed once you're done. New York Puzzle Company jigsaw puzzles are full-on art pieces just waiting to be put together.

New York Puzzle Company - Loré Pemberton Cold Hollow

New York Puzzle Company - New Yorker Bodega Cat

New York Puzzle Company - Harry Potter Flying Keys

New York Puzzle Company - Victo Ngai Utopia

How Do You Know if a Brand Has Quality Puzzles?

It's always worth researching a brand when you come across a puzzle that interests you to learn more about them. Quite a few companies will have further details about them on their website to read so you can have a better idea about who you're buying from. Another great way to learn more about a brand is by reading reviews or comments from fellow puzzlers online who have bought from the brand previously. Doing this can help you make a good judgement call about a brand and if they're worth your time and money. New York Puzzle Comap

What is the best piece count for puzzles?

Puzzles come in a pretty wide variety of piece counts, but some of the most common are 300, 500, and 1000-piece puzzles. Choosing what piece count is right for you depends on a mixture of how good you are at puzzles, how much time you have, and whether or not you have a dedicated space to do puzzles. Lower piece counts are usually better for casual puzzlers and kids, but higher piece counts are better for adults and challenge seekers. That being said, the most common piece counts you'll see from the best jigsaw puzzle brands are 500 and 1000-piece puzzles.

What type of material is good for quality puzzles?

For most quality jigsaw puzzles, a sturdy cardboard base is what you'll find used as the material. You can usually judge a puzzle's quality by just how sturdy and thick the cardboard is. Puzzle cardboard (also known as chipboard) comes in a pretty wide variety of thicknesses and this can affect how easily the puzzle fits together. Lower-quality puzzles will usually use thinner base coardboard resulting in flimsier pieces that don't have that same 'click' when you put them together. Outside of cardboard, wood can be a good material for puzzles. However depending on the type of wood used you might end up with chipped or splintered pieces. Most of the time high-quality cardboard is what you should be looking for.

In the world of jigsaw puzzles, there are multiple dimensions in which you could be working with. 2D puzzles are the standard flat versions most folks are used to, but the 3D variety brings the puzzle into model kit territory. If you're trying to choose which type of puzzle to buy, it really just comes down to whether or not you want to display the end result. 3D puzzles are great if you're looking to build something to keep on a shelf or a desk, whereas 2D puzzles are great for framing and hanging on your wall. If you're just looking for a jigsaw puzzle to put together at your leisure and then stuff back in the box, 2D is the way to go.

If you're interested in 3D puzzles, we recommend you check out some of the coolest book nook kits for adults . These are designed to sit on your shelf among a book collection. You can also see our guide to the best 3D puzzle alternatives to popular LEGO sets if you're looking for something specific.

Puzzling can certainly be an expensive hobby if you do a lot of puzzling. Because of this there are a lot of really cheap jigsaw puzzles available at online retailers like Amazon from brands you've likely never heard of. The general rule of thumb is that a cheaper puzzle will most likely be lower-quality than a more expensive one. This is because higher-quality puzzles are usually made of higher-quality materials (thicker cardboard, wood, etc). That being said, not every expensive puzzle is going to automatically be better quality than something cheaper. It all depends on the brand and what licensing has gone into the making of that puzzle.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the guides and commerce teams here at IGN.

articles.title: 'Similar Art Styles Make the Comparisons Inevitable' — Palworld and Pokémon Fans Are Arguing Over Whether New Whale Pal Panthalus Copies Kyogre
articles.summary: Palworld and Pokémon fans are arguing over whether a new whale Pal called Panthalus copies the Pokémon, Kyogre.
articles.body:
Palworld and Pokémon fans are arguing over whether a new whale Pal called Panthalus copies the Pokémon, Kyogre.

Palworld creature Panthalus is a massive legendary blue-green whale with a white belly, flared fins and tribal-like markings across its body, plus a large bronze decoration. Beloved Pokémon Kyogre, meanwhile, is a legendary blue whale with a white belly, flared fins and tribal markings across its body, with no bronze decoration.

Writing on social media, some fans have said that the design of Panthalus is "clearly inspired" by Kyogre, even if the concept of a mythical whale is not unique to Pokémon. One fan dubbed the design as "brazen," though others said it looked "legally distinct" enough.

"I feel like the similar art styles make the comparisons inevitable," tweeted video game content creator Josh Scorcher. "Like, Game Freak doesn't own the concept of a legendary/divine whale creature... But you have to be incredibly dishonest to not immediately think of Kyogre when you see this."

Others, however, have dismissed the comparison. "Literally the only thing they have in common is that they're both whales," one fan said . "Panthalus looks NOTHING like Kyorge," another added . "Concept is there, but I can easily visually distinguish them."

oh my god the people saying panthalus doesnt even RESEMBLE kyogre are coping so unbelievably hard bro pic.twitter.com/1Ph4IJR39Q — Decaticon (@Decaticon) July 14, 2026

oh my god the people saying panthalus doesnt even RESEMBLE kyogre are coping so unbelievably hard bro pic.twitter.com/1Ph4IJR39Q

This pal is clearly inspired by Kyogre which isn't inherently a bad thing. However because palworld creatures are mostly inspired by pokemon it makes their designs feel pretty uninspired. Palworld's designs would greatly benefit from taking more inspiration outside of pokemon pic.twitter.com/dA5Jv0waP9 — doodlelotl (@Doodlelot) July 14, 2026

This pal is clearly inspired by Kyogre which isn't inherently a bad thing. However because palworld creatures are mostly inspired by pokemon it makes their designs feel pretty uninspired. Palworld's designs would greatly benefit from taking more inspiration outside of pokemon pic.twitter.com/dA5Jv0waP9

Sind sich zu ähnlich⁉️ Panthalus 🐳, ein Pal aus Palworld von Pocketpair Inc. & Kyogre 🐋, ein Pokemon von Gamefreak / Nintendo #pokemon #palworld pic.twitter.com/2XQhZXWNvv — PokéTen @Eurofurence 30 (@poketen_) July 15, 2026

Sind sich zu ähnlich⁉️ Panthalus 🐳, ein Pal aus Palworld von Pocketpair Inc. & Kyogre 🐋, ein Pokemon von Gamefreak / Nintendo #pokemon #palworld pic.twitter.com/2XQhZXWNvv

Panthalus' introduction comes just as fans discovered that several other Pal species have quietly had their designs changed in Palworld's big 1.0 update . Despite hundreds of other additions and tweaks being listed in developer Pocketpair's patch notes, there was curiously no mention of alterations to Verdash, Robinquill, Fengallop, and Grintale, which previously displayed more distinct similarities to familiar Pokémon species Cinderace, Decidueye, Cobalion, and Galarian Meowth.

IGN contacted Pocketpair for comment about these changes, but received no response.

Comparisons between Palworld's Pal designs and Pokémon are nothing new, of course, and fans have been pointing out similarities between species since before Palworld's original launch, when many accused Pocketpair of "ripping off" Pokémon designs.

And of course, all of this comes amid the ongoing legal battle between The Pokémon Company and Pocketpair over the use of patents, which seemingly prompted the latter to make gameplay changes in order to nullify its claims. A judgment is expected later this year .

Palworld's 1.0 launch landed earlier this month, finally bringing the game out of early access. Pocketpair said at the time that it would not raise the game's price beyond $29.99 as Palworld has "become a success beyond our wildest dreams." That statement likely reflects the fact that more than 40 million players have dipped their paws into Palworld since its early access launch.

Our Palworld Interactive Map has been updated for 1.0, including Watchtower Locations , so you can make sure to uncover everything new. We’ve also got a guide to 1.0 Pal Breeding Combos and How to Get Hardwood , plus the Best 1.0 Mounts to Catch in Order , and the Fastest Flying Mounts in 1.0 .

articles.title: The Original Pokémon Series Is Now Streaming on Disney+ — So Where Are All of the Episodes?
articles.summary: The original Pokémon TV series is officially streaming on Disney+. Some of it, at least.
articles.body:
The original Pokémon TV series is officially streaming on Disney+ . Some of it, at least.

Of the 80ish total episodes that comprise the original Indigo League arc , only 27 are now available on Disney+. That's not an entirely random number — the first season of Pokémon was split into three parts when it was brought to DVD in North America, and Disney's episode count lines up with what was included on Viz Media’s first compilation.

Netflix, which has long been the streaming home for most of the Pokémon series , continues to have the first 52 episodes. That number matches how the series was originally split up for annual North American broadcast schedules.

Unlike Netflix, which goes with the specific "Indigo League" title, the episodes on Disney+ can be found under the arc's broader title, “Pokémon the Series: The Beginning.” Both streaming services skip over the original 18th episode, “ Beauty and the Beach ,” which only aired a few times in the U.S. after some heavy editing.

You're not entirely out of luck if you're looking for the full 80-episode arc. Those last 26 episodes are available to stream for free with ads on YouTube and Tubi , and are also included in Warner Home Video's revamped DVD release from 2014.

Disney+ was already streaming most of the more recent Sun & Moon seasons as well as a small selection of Pokémon movies, including The Rise of Darkrai and Zoroark: Master of Illusions . The addition of the original arc marks the streamer’s first major move with the franchise since acquiring the streaming license earlier this year.

Disney also picked up the broadcast rights for the original series, meaning Pokémon is officially back on Disney XD schedules .

The Pokémon TV series has become pretty closely associated with Netflix, with the streamer even producing its own original series with the franchise, Pokémon Concierge . It’s not entirely clear what else Disney plans to do with its newly acquired streaming and broadcast rights, and whether we’ll ever get the full Indigo League arc (let alone the full series) on either streaming platform.

Pokémon as a whole is currently celebrating its 30th anniversary, which has naturally been a ripe occasion for announcements across all of the franchise's iterations. We're talking new TCG releases , plenty of Pokémon Go events , and even some LEGO sets .

Somewhat ironically, the mainline Pokemon games are actually skipping 2026, but we did get our hands on what I consider one of the best cozy games of the modern generation, Pokémon Pokopia . We also got our first look at Gen 10 , Winds and Waves, which included a glimpse at the three new starters .

Disney+ continues to chug along in its own right, though it no longer openly reports the number of subscribers across its particularly large number of plans and bundles . The company has recently been focused on diversifying what it offers through the Disney+ app, having just inked a deal with TikTok to bring user-made shorts to the service. The possibility of a free, ad-supported streaming option was mentioned during the company's most recent earnings call , but in the era of endless price hikes , I wouldn’t get too optimistic.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Krispy Kreme Is Getting 6 New Pokémon-Themed Donuts
articles.summary: Krispy Kreme has announced a Pokémon doughnut collection that will be available for a limited time starting August 18.
articles.body:
Krispy Kreme has announced a Pokémon doughnut collection that will be available for a limited time starting August 18.

The collection, which is exclusive to U.S. and Canadian locations, will include six doughnuts total. Five are themed after specific Pokémon, including all three Gen 1 starters and two more Kanto region favorites. The sixth doughnut is an interpretation of the classic Poké Ball.

The doughnuts will be available for purchase individually or as a ‘Specialty Dozen Pack’ in select Krispy Kreme stores and through the Krispy Kreme app. A separate six-pack that skips out on Squirtle and Bulbasaur, replacing them with plain glazed doughnuts, will be available at other retailers like Walmart, Kroger, and Publix.

If you opt for the full Specialty Dozen, you’ll get a special, limited-edition Pokémon box. Krispy Kreme will also be offering five different Pokémon-themed cups for serving 'Original Glazed Gold Dots,' its version of doughnut holes.

That’s not all. Next Saturday, August 22, anyone who wears Pokémon merch to a participating Krispy Kreme location will get a free original glazed doughnut. It would have been nice if the freebie was Pokémon-themed, but a deal is a deal.

Preorders for the full 12-pack have already opened online , suggesting the doughnut company may have some concerns about potential stock. Yes, the Pokémon scalping problem now extends far beyond the trading card game. This may explain why a press release from Krispy Kreme only indicates that the Pokémon-themed collection will be available for a ‘limited time’ instead of having a clear end date.

If you'd like to plan your Pokémon journey sooner rather than later, you can check for participating locations on the Krispy Kreme website .

The Krispy Kreme collection is the latest addition to a long list of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary celebrations. Throughout 2026, we’ve seen merch collaborations with companies like Puma , some beautiful new guide books , and the release of a whopping 20 Pokemon-themed LEGO sets . The Pokémon trading card game will also be getting a special 30th anniversary product drop later this year.

While we won’t be getting a mainline Pokémon game, we did get our first look at Gen 10 , Winds and Waves, which is slated for 2027. We also got our hands on a new spin-off, Pokemon Pokopia, a Switch 2 exclusive we called an “enjoyable, personality-packed building simulator ” in our 9/10 review .

articles.title: The Pokémon Center Just Dropped Its 2026 Halloween Collection
articles.summary: The Pokémon Center just dropped its Halloween Collection for 2026, with new apparel and decor featuring Gengar, Mimikyu, Umbreon, and... Golett?
articles.body:
The Pokémon Center just dropped its Halloween Collection for 2026. The new releases, which are already available to purchase online , include a mix of spooky-themed decorations, apparel, and kitchenware featuring fan-favorite Pokémon. The company is also seemingly getting ahead of the winter holiday season with new ornaments and snow globes.

Pok é mon Center Reveals 2026 Halloween Collection

The Pokémon Company has been celebrating the franchise’s 30th anniversary with a ridiculous amount of drops and announcements . This is one collection I always look forward to, however, because I’m a huge fan of the Ghost types that are typically featured.

It shouldn't come as any surprise that the Poké-star of this year’s drop is Gengar, who technically predates the Ghost type itself . That guy’s been getting a ridiculous amount of merch love recently. Other featured Pokémon include Mimikyu, Mewtwo, one of my all-time favorites, Misdreavus, and… Golett ? That one honestly caught me off guard.

On the decor side, I'm a big fan of the Umbreon and Espeon statues. I want the ethereal Eevee-lution duo guarding my house (apartment, but let me pretend) at all times. These are the same "made to look like stone" style as the previously released Cubone and Mimikyu statues that have been out of stock all year.

There’s a spread of more functional ‘pumpkin Pokémon’-themed items like tea-light holders and mugs, which I personally think are a bit jarring to look at. One thing that certainly isn't spooky is the Ditto candy holder. I, like presumably many people, recently rediscovered my adoration for Ditto through Pokémon Pokopia , and actually love how this thing is used to house tons of plushies in the promotional images .

The new apparel generally falls into the ‘cozy’ category, with a mix of sweaters, pajamas, and even bath robes almost entirely in adult sizes. The knit Gengar cardigan is a personal highlight, with a darker spiral pattern that's making me want to kick off my annual rewatch of The Nightmare Before Christmas.

Speaking of, the drop also includes a new batch of ornaments. I guess Halloween is close enough to the winter festivities.

The collection varies widely in terms of pricing, with the ornaments being the cheapest at $16.99, followed by Halloween-themed Pokémon window clings for $19.99. The most expensive new release is the luxurious Gengar bath robe, listed at $69.99.

articles.title: Control Resonant Made Me Feel Foolish For Ever Doubting It — IGN First
articles.summary: I played two brand new Control Resonant missions and feel foolish for ever doubting it. Our final preview:
articles.body:
I first played Control Resonant back in June, having made my way through the same couple of hours as my colleague, Mitchell Saltzman, detailed in IGN’s first preview . Much like him, I had a great time getting to grips with the series’ newfound melee systems, hacking and slashing away at the Hiss threats that have broken out into the sequel’s open Manhattan. But I’ll admit that introduction did leave me a little wary of whether the dial may have been turned a little too much to the action side of things, and wondering if its open-world playground was merely there to serve as a place to grind XP and hone combat skills. As the studio steps further into the world of the action RPG, is it necessary to tread ground that won’t click with me in the same way Remedy’s previous games did?

So, I stepped into my exclusive two-hour-long demo of Control Resonant hoping to see more of what I love so much about Remedy’s output — unrivalled world-building, consistently surprising level design, and simply being shown things I haven’t seen before. Thankfully, I was not disappointed.

Do not fear, there’s plenty of weirdness here. Even the fast travel points are mysteriously placed doors that conjure looping snapshots of the surrounding scene within their frames when opened. This is a New York of Remedy’s design, one that takes familiar art deco architecture and bends it into the studio’s own image. Yes, there are flashes of other science fiction worlds here — one note I read even playfully references Inception and its folding city — but the Finnish developer firmly puts its singular stamp down wherever it can.

I felt it most keenly in the first of two brand new missions I got to play, which took me deep into the Big Apple’s subway system in search of the Reach ability, Resonant’s grapple hook equivalent. The Metro Vault is one of many “dungeons” where traversal abilities are learned, but they also push the story forward in interesting ways — often showing glimpses into protagonist Dylan’s relationship with his sister, Jesse, and their intertwining tales that have led to this moment. They’re a prime example of Remedy’s well-honed ability to layer each of its levels with both narrative and gameplay purpose, all while putting things on your TV that you’ve not quite seen before.

Here, in the middle of Metro Madness, trains hurtle across the screen from every direction, showing no respect for the laws of physics. Dylan is able to shift the gravitational pull of the tunnels at will; With the press of a button, he can make the ceiling his floor in order to better navigate the screeching obstacles that rattle along each perilous passage. It’s a neat bit of puzzle platforming that makes you question each and every leap of faith. When faced with a gaping drop into the unknown, in most games the wrong call would be to fall all the way down. But Control Resonant doesn’t like to play by the rules, with the void acting as the critical path. Curiosity is rewarded in both its linear and open areas.

These winding corridors are also full of Mold enemies, a returning faction you can read all about in my deep dive into Resonant’s enemies. They pose a different threat to the much more common Hiss, proving much harder to directly damage due to their armored casings. But while you need to find and exploit their weakness, I appreciate that there’s no single solution to effectively taking down an enemy. While the fire-sparking Heat Wave and Heat Aura abilities can melt through the Mold’s armour plating, if you haven’t equipped either, you can do exactly what I did and use your shape-shifting weapon, The Aberrant, to conjure a giant hammer and bash their hardened outer layer off, then shift to a blade form to slice up their fungal insides. This flexible approach to combat means minimal time is spent in menus crafting builds, and more time toe-to-toe with the threats you’ll be taking down with them.

Speaking of which, the second mission I was dropped into featured the Central Resonant, one of the sequel’s big bosses. But before I could battle it, I first had to find its lair. Working out the building it called home was simple enough — a towering smokestack stretching improbably high into the sky revealed a factory as such a place — but getting in there and finding its exact location within those walls was another challenge altogether. To do so, I had to fend off a few bothersome Hiss, which I did so using the satisfying tactic of bulldozing into larger enemies with my trusty rock shield, which builds up enough of their stun meter to allow me to deliver a slick finisher with The Aberrant's dual-blade form.

Over the course of my few hours with Resonant, I can’t say I ever felt anything approaching boredom with its combat, which consistently delivers a feel-good power trip in each encounter. Key to this is Remedy’s decision to kill off all minor grunts in an area after you’ve defeated the larger enemies within a horde. It helps keep the game’s momentum going, without bogging you down in battles that could otherwise outstay their welcome.

Once the streets were clear, I could get on with solving the puzzle needed in order to open the factory’s doors. This involved stabbing a nearby electrical power source with Dylan’s blade, which can hold a charge for a limited time, and scuttling as quickly as I could to an unpowered cube in need of energy. I’d previously engaged with a more complex version of this puzzle, which had me transporting power across roads and rooftops between multiple generators, which put my traversal skills to the test. It’s encouraging to see that Control Resonant’s open world challenges won’t be limited solely to combat, but also test your mental muscles, too.

A prime example of this was when I came into contact with an Altered Item — everyday objects that have developed paranatural properties in the Control Universe. In this case, it was a Polaroid camera that disappeared with a flash and snap every time I approached it. In order to get close to it, I needed to find an alternative way into the room and sneak up on it from behind. Doing so made it vanish again, but this time kicking off a whole new side questline that seemed to insinuate I’d be meeting this camera many more times on my travels across New York. It’s these sorts of strange sojourns that allayed any fears I had that Remedy was going too action-heavy in this sequel. Rest assured, there’s still plenty of that weirdness and puzzle-solving that the original featured so heavily.

But back to the mission at hand. Upon entering the factory, I ventured down into its depths only to be met with a series of steaming hot pipes blocking my progress. So, into its intertwining tunnels I went in search of a way to clear a path. This led to a cluster of intense battles, side paths full of upgrade materials, and plenty of lore pertaining to horrors that took place here – horrors that resulted in a sixty-foot-tall magma monster living in the factory’s bowels. It’s the backstory I found here that made this whole area come to life for me, as some of that trademark Remedy dark humour pierced through an otherwise desperate situation.

The boss at the end of this tale would be the biggest challenge I would face in my time with Control Resonant. A giant volcanic-rock-covered man, it struck a powerful, tortured form, with pipes protruding from its back like steaming spikes and a screaming maw that constantly spewed molten lava. It took me a couple of attempts to take it down, once I’d found out the key was to literally never stay still. This is a mantra carried across all of Control Resonant, but this boss fight really hits that point home. As much as half of the arena’s floor can be covered in highly damaging lava at any time, so dashing, hovering, or using the aforementioned shield is necessary in order to get in close. Once within striking distance, you’ll want to get stuck in (without being greedy) before your foe starts splurging all over again. The pace never lets off, so it’s a good sign that Remedy appears to have judged each boss fight’s duration well - none of my encounters ever felt that they lasted too long.

That relatively fleeting fight time means there’s no checkpointing. Instead, a slight reprieve is offered by a burst of healing, triggered by reducing a boss’s health bar down to a couple of predetermined points, each marked by a blue dot. It’s a really smart way of further encouraging that “attack is the best form of defense” mindset that runs through Resonant’s design, and a clever method of not flooding boss arenas with annoying smaller enemies who are there purely for you to farm health from. From my limited experience of the sequel’s biggest encounters, it really seems a step forward in terms of boss design for Remedy this time around.

But, as I said, despite being heavily influenced by action RPGs, there’s so much more to Control Resonant than combat. During my brief poke around New York, I stumbled across little puzzles to complete, scanning devices to turn on in order to reveal locations of other activities, and many, many pieces of world-building lore. That storytelling was most keenly felt in a visit to the city’s central FBC Field Office. Here I bumped into familiar faces from the first game, read classified documents relating to corrupting forces plaguing Manhattan, and even took part in the first few steps of a side mission relating to a corpse whose head had mysteriously exploded — just another day in the Federal Bureau of Control.

It all makes for a very exciting mix. Even if the edge-of-your-seat combat is often the star of the show, slick platforming, clever puzzles, and best-in-class worldbuilding each have their space to shine. Control Resonant is not quite Remedy going full open-world, but it certainly looks set to be an impressive expansion of all of the ideas that made the original so engaging, with none of what makes the studio’s games so memorable lost in the upsizing. Simply put, my initial fears have all but been extinguished, and now I can’t wait for September 24.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: 4 Penny Coffins Lets You Play 19th-Century Detective – Or a 10-Foot Demon Ripping Friends in Half
articles.summary: Other Ocean’s 4 Penny Coffins blends Among Us with Jack the Ripper in an 1888 Whitechapel social investigation game featuring 8-player and solo modes.
articles.body:
4 Penny Coffins is Jack the Ripper Meets Among Us, with a little bit of Psychonauts thrown in for fun. In the upcoming social investigation game, up to 8 players hunt a hidden murderer through lies, shifting alibis, and hard evidence . One of the players is the Ripper, a “gleeful demon concealed behind a facade of humanity,” stalking the winding alleys and rotting byways of 1888 London.

Ahead of IGN debuting 4 Penny Coffins’s gameplay teaser during gamescom 2026, which you can see in the player below, I spoke to Other Ocean Interactive Marketing Manager Jared Petty about the game’s mechanics, unique style (think stylized gore on top of monochromatic photographs), and Tim Schafer-inspired humor.

“It's a goddamn blast,” Petty says. “Four Penny Coffins; I've rarely had more fun playing a game with other people. A long time ago I was talking to Tim Schafer and I was asking him about humor in video games. Tim's opinion is that humor in video games is the easiest thing in the world because to paraphrase, ‘Our medium was built on a little yellow man that eats dots being chased by ghosts.’

“Humor and horror have always gone together so well. [Four Penny Coffins] having a multiplayer mode and being a very socially-oriented one creates all kinds of opportunities. Our philosophy was that the comical allows you to laugh so you don't scream.”

Petty says that the game’s humor translates directly into a multiplayer experience where you’re rewarded for trying to work together, but only if you want to.

“If you love trolling your friends, it's a beautiful game to play,” Petty says. “Our multiplayer ‘Ripper’ mode is class-based. All of you have different forensic abilities and are hunting the Ripper before they commit another murder. The fun part is one of you is the Ripper. So seven of you are using fingerprint and blood splatter analysis, photographing things, talking to witnesses, following photoprints, and doing all kinds of detective stuff, one of you screwing with that and occasionally turning into a giant 10-foot demon monster ripping people in half.”

Petty says that, while the “Ripper” mode allows you to work with your friends to figure out which one of you is 19th-century-inspired holy terror, the game’s solo “Magistrate” mode takes a different approach.

“It’s way more Sherlock Holmes-y,” Petty says. “Since you're there on your own, you've got a group of suspects locked up in a jail and you know one of them is the Ripper. You just don't know which one. So you're using tools from all the classes to go out and try to solve the mystery within a time limit. You make your choice and if you are wrong, you are penalized. You have three opportunities for your demerits. You take all your deductive reasoning and all your clues within that time limit, you bring it back, and you’ve got to hang somebody.”

Beyond the game mechanics, Petty says that the setting and style of 4 Penny Coffins is intended to help it stand out.

“I think you can see the influence in the graphic novel From Hell,” Petty says. “4 Penny Coffins is mostly a game that's in black and white until something [red and] violent happens. The game is built around an imaginative interpretation of a very dystopian time in 1888 Whitechapel London, which is where Jack the Ripper was. We wanted to create a sense of abstraction that was evocative of the age. We said, ‘What would an old woodcut newspaper brought to life look like? What would a moving grainy photo from the period look like?’ Our studio director, Chris Navarro, said ‘It's just gotta look cool.’”

When 4 Penny Coffins is released, Petty hopes players appreciate the care that went into crafting its story, mechanics, and style. But while the game promises tons of murder, violence, and mayhem, Petty says you don’t have to be a fan of the horror genre in order to enjoy it.

“It's just a great game for your friends and on your own. It's just really kind of a chill mental exercise, almost a puzzle. If you like puzzle games, you're going to love [it].”

For more from gamescom, be sure to check out everything that was revealed during Opening Night Live.

If you’ve never used an electric shaver, you really are missing out. They’re smooth, they’re satisfying, and quite often they’ll net you a closer shave than a manual razor that gets duller in days.

Thankfully, Philips has an array of excellent options, and they’re seeing decent discounts right now at Amazon - including a whopping 51% off the i9000 Prestige Ultra, which sounds like it should be a car rather than something you use on your face.

We’ve already pointed out the OneBlade is seeing a great discount, but it’s not alone in that regard - and there’s something for just about any budget right now with these discounts at Amazon.

Take the Philips Electric Shaver Series 3000X , for example. It’s a sleek, comfortable device that would usually set you back £54.99, now just £44.99.

Not the biggest discount, admittedly, but for a first electric razor it’s really hard to go wrong. It offers a comfortable, clean shave that won’t leave marks despite using 27 self-sharpening blades, and is guaranteed for two years.

Those blades cup up to 55,000 times per minute to keep your shave steady and consistent, and the three heads can flex in four directions to match the contours of your face.

Next up is the Philips Electric Shaver Series 5000 , which, again, has 27 self-sharpening blades as well as a clip-on trimmer to maintain your ‘tache, trim your sideburns, or shape up your eyebrows (if you’re feeling brave).

Unlike the aforementioned model, its heads move 360 degrees to help with comfort while shaving, plus there’s a display that shows when it needs cleaning, charging, or the heads need replacing. It’s now £74.99, down 53% from its RRP of £159.99.

Looking for something even fancier for your face? The Philips Shaver i9000 Prestige Ultra (you know it’s good because ‘Prestige’ and ‘Ultra’ are in the name) usually sells for £649.99 - you could buy a whole new face for that.

Still, it’s an Amazon Exclusive, award-winning shaver that has a seven-year warranty and offers a 20% more precise shave than a manual razor. It’s now down to £319.99, marking a 51% discount on that eye-watering RRP.

Whether it’s a big social occasion, a job interview, or just everyday maintenance, it’s clear there’s never been a better time to pick up a new shaver and revitalise your look.

articles.title: Chess.com launched a poker site and is planning even more classic games
articles.summary: Chess.com’s new poker site, Gambit, is its first expansion, and now it’s working on launching sites for more games, like go, backgammon, and mahjong.
articles.body: Chess.com has done one thing, and one thing very well, for almost 20 years, but now it’s going beyond its domain name. The biggest name in online chess quietly launched its first companion site in beta back in May: Gambit, a free online poker website where players can learn the game without risking any real money. Now Gambit’s ready to really get the ball rolling with its first livestreamed event and collaborations with content creators, and Chess.com is planning to branch out into even more games from here. Chess.com’s chief growth officer, Albert Cheng, told The Verge the company chose poker for its first companion site because, like chess, it has learning and social elements on top of just playing the game. He also promised there will never be real-money gambling on Gambit, saying, “Real money is the problem we built Gambit to get away from, the whole industry makes money when beginners lose. We’d rather build a place where people can actually learn.” Gambit will look familiar to anyone who’s used Chess.com. It borrows the same design style and includes similar play modes, like bot matches, games with friends, tournaments, a review mode for studying your past games, and a learning mode. Gambit even includes Chess.com’s bot characters, with matching skill levels — I immediately recognized “Martin,” the lowest skill level bot from Chess.com, who is also the lowest skill level bot on Gambit. [Image: [Image: Chess.com also developed its own Elo-style rating system for Gambit. Cheng explained in an interview with The Verge that the rating system serves as the main motivator for players to improve: “You’re not gambling your own hard-earned money necessarily, so the stakes are lower from that standpoint, but you need something to counterbalance it that you care about, and that keeps the ecosystem in play, and keeps the poker that’s on Gambit reasonably high-quality.” The rating system is also the backbone of Gambit’s paid subscription for access to premium learning features, following the same model Chess.com uses. “Our primary business model of Chess.com is a subscription, but most people play Chess.com for free,” Cheng said. “They subscribe to get unlimited access to review their games and to get unlimited puzzles, lessons, et cetera.” A reliable rating system allows players to track their improvement, potentially motivating them to pay for those premium features. [Image: [Image: Rating systems are also at the heart of Chess’s next move. Chess.com is now looking to expand into even more classic games, including go, backgammon, and mahjong. Like Gambit, Chess.com is developing Elo-style rating systems for these games, as well. Cheng didn’t say when the new sites will launch but that “development is moving quite rapidly” on them, using the same playbook he used for Gambit. AI is a key reason Chess.com was finally able to expand into other games after nearly 20 years, according to Cheng. He and one other employee took Gambit from prototype to launch within a year, partly with help from AI, mainly for coding tasks. “I think the biggest advantage that it’s provided is essentially being able to read our existing codebase and our design system and apply consistent patterns to how we develop Chess.com over to a different platform and do so quickly,” Cheng said. He went on to add that there were also a lot of areas where AI struggles, such as brand and feature design. “I think that’s the best ultimate use of AI is that ultimately it’s going to be a blend, right?” Cheng said, adding, “Just because code is easier to write doesn’t mean that you just let it run on its own, but it certainly is a superpower in getting things off the ground.” Cheng also said the version of Gambit that’s live at the time of writing has “zero or close to zero” AI-created assets, which were used in early prototypes. According to Cheng, without help from AI, getting another site up and running would have required a bigger team or “would have been a lot more disruptive to the status quo of building and growing Chess.” Now that a “small, scrappy” team can get a new platform off the ground much faster, it’s opened the door for Chess.com to dip into more games, starting with poker. As Chess.com plans its next move, Cheng says they’re focusing on games with “both that classic durability plus the community around it,” like chess. Now that Gambit has launched, Cheng’s leaning into the community and social side of the platform more, following Chess.com’s lead, and getting content creators more involved. On August 31st at 12PM ET / 9AM PT, Gambit’s livestreaming its Gambit Cup for the first time on Twitch and YouTube with Chess.com co-founder Danny Rensch and chess content creator Alexandra Botez.

articles.title: PSA: Nintendo Switch 2 Gets a $50 Price Increase on Tuesday
articles.summary: Nintendo is raising the price of the Switch 2 to $500 on September 1, meaning this is your last chance to get one before the hike.
articles.body:
Compared to Sony and Microsoft , Nintendo has done an admirable job of keeping the price of the Switch 2 reasonably low amid rising component prices. But not even Mario is immune to market forces, and Nintendo is raising the Switch 2’s price by $50 on September 1. So, starting Tuesday, you’ll have to fork out $500 for a new hybrid console instead of the current MSRP of $450. In other words, if you’re thinking of picking up a Switch 2, this is your last chance to do so before the price hike.

When it comes to buying a Switch 2, you used to have more options than you do today. Previously, you could buy the console all by itself, or bundled with a game. There was even a bundle that let you choose among three first-party games. As we creep toward the price hike, however, all of the bundles have vanished from retailers. Your only reasonably priced option now is wither to buy a Switch 2 new or refurbished .

New Switch 2 consoles are available at all the usual retailers ( see at Amazon ). Refurbished Switch 2s are available at several retailers, but the best deal going right now is a “Grade A” refurbished unit at Woot for $399.99 . That’s $50 less than the current price of a new Switch 2, and it’s the best deal going if you don’t mind refurbished hardware.

Woot, by the way, is owned by Amazon, so you can rest assured it’s a legit retailer. I’ve bought many things from Woot and never had any problems.

Nintendo has announced it will introduce two new Switch 2 bundles after the price hike. One includes a copy of Mario Kart World . It will be available in “late September” and cost $549.99. The other includes Nintendo Switch Sports Resort . It will cost $529.99 and will be out October 22, the day that game comes out.

Both bundles will include three months of Nintendo Switch Online, and offer slight discounts versus buying the items individually. But neither bundle will save you more than $50, meaning your best bet is still to buy before the price goes up.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Every Cosmere Tabletop Game Based on Brandon Sanderson's Epic Book Universe
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson’s Cosmere universe has delighted readers ever since his first book, Elantris, released more than two decades ago. Now, it spans over 20 books with more in the works and even a new movie and television series looming based on the immensely popular Mistborn and Stormlight Archive books, respectively. Over the years, the tales of Vin, Kaladin, and the Shards of Adonalsium have made the jump from page to the tabletop as well, with a number of board games and tabletop roleplaying games having been released for players to enjoy.

This list showcases all of the tabletop games that you can currently experience, along with the ones that we know about!

Brotherwise Games , publishers of games like Boss Monster, Night of the Ninja, and Call to Adventure, this studio is the official partner for Sanderson’s Cosmere when it comes to the board game space. So far they have released a solid mix of titles with something for nearly all ages of Cosmere fans, with some of their biggest stuff still on the way.

Call to Adventure: The Stormlight Archive

Built on Brotherwises’ “Call to Adventure” board game system, Call to Adventure: The Stormlight Archive asks players to create the most epic and interesting character they can. A bit of an engine builder, you will be drafting cards to build out your character's history, motivation, and destiny while balancing their morality, all culminating at the end in your own personal hero’s journey and scoring points. Complete quests by rolling nifty rune slabs, balance on the thin line between hero and anti-hero through three rounds with the winner being whoever has the most dragic/awesome character backstory (aka has the most points). Not only can CtA: The Stormlight Archive is not only a solid game, but also a great character-building exercise which is perfect for the next game…

Stormlight Handbook, Cosmere RPG Core Rulebook

Stormlight Archive Stonewalkers Adventure

For the tabletop roleplaying fans, the Cosmere RPG gives you the tools and systems to live out your dreams in the world of Roshar. Whether you want to walk down the path of becoming a knight radiant, take on the form of a singer, or perhaps just a simple soldier trying to survive, the Cosmere RPG gives you the tools to do all that and more. Your character’s motivation and the story you and your friends create in the Cosmere are the driving force behind this system and Brotherwise is just getting started with the world of Scadrail and its Allomancers coming soon as well. A host of products are available, from the Stormlight Handbook with all you need to run a campaign on Roshar, the Stonewalkers Adventure for a constructed story, and even a welcoming Starter Set if you just want to get a taste.

Showcasing events and characters from the first book of the Mistborn series, The Final Empire, the Mistborn: The Deckbuilding Game puts 1-4 players in the roles of beloved characters including Vin and Kelsier. Players will build out their decks from an available pull of cards while also learning and improving their ability to burn metals as allomancers - the signature magic of the world of Scadriel. All the while, working to become strong enough to complete missions and take out the other players, or the Lord Ruler himself in an optional cooperative game mode. With gorgeous artwork and solid deckbuilding at its core, this game is a great buy for fans of Mistborn, and it will be getting an expansion soon as well, that adds new characters, powers, and highlight moments from the second book, the Well of Ascension!

The lightest of the main three Cosmere games from Brotherwise, Shards of Creation is a ticktaking card game where depending on which of the Shards of Adonalsium get picked can greatly change how you play. Each of the Shards included in the base game: Autonomy, Cultivation, Devotion, Dominion, Honor, Odium, Preservation and Ruin feature unique powers that can both help or hurt you as you form sets of suits for end game scoring. Featuring canonical depictions of the vessels of the Shards (up to a point, anyway), some of which first appearing in Shards of Creation, make this a great option for both fans of the Cosmere but also folks who just enjoy a good trick-taking game to bust out when they have a little time on their hands.

Prior to Brotherwise securing their partnership with Sanderson, another group, publisher Crafty Games, had a go adapting the author’s popular Mistborn series for the tabletop.

Set during the first book, House War is a resource management game where as opposed to taking up the Mistcloak of a specific character, each player assumes the role of one of the factions around the city. The aim is to keep down the unrest by solving issues around the Empire, competing to earn the most favor. This game is less about burning metals and pushing through the mists and more about making deals, but House War has the twist where its possible the player with either the lowest or highest score could potentially win. There are also rules that allow shorter games to play out in 60-90 minutes or longer games between two and three hours long, give you and your group flexibility to slot this in either as a bit of a filler game or be the main game of the night. An expansion, “The Siege of Luthadel” expands the game and sets the game during the second novel and attempts to hold everything together.

The first TTRPG set in the world of the Cosmere, released first back in summer of 2012, this tabletop adventure system lets players build Nobels, Skaa, Terrismen and even Kandra in the world of Scadrial to live out their stories during the first era of the Mistborn saga. Developed by Crafty Games, this d6 based system is far more narrative-driven where factors like Destiny and Tragedy factor into character creation. There are a host of expansions and additional books that were released for MDA including Terris: Wrought of Copper that focuses on the Terris people and Feruchemists, Alloy of Law, Skaa: Tin & Ash, Alloy of Law: Masks of the past, and Nobels: The Golden Mandate.

If you are still hungry for more, Brotherwise Games should have you covered to get your Cosmere tabletop kick for some time yet, with a number of games and expansions on the horizon. The Mistborn deck builder has its first expansion, “ The Well of Ascension ,” featuring a new cooperative mode where players need to work together to defend the city of Luthadel from a horde of Koloss, and more pulled from the second book of era 2 Mistborn.

Staying on the Allomancer train, the Cosmere RPG will also soon be getting its Mistborn books , letting players create their own mistborns and allomancers while taking part in adventures set in both the first and second eras of the series!

Lastly, later this fall, Brotherwise will be bringing the Stormlight Archive to Kickstarter with their War for Roshar board game. Previously covered here on IGN with an exclusive preview , this is a heavy area control / euro title that will see up to four players facing off against either on the side of Honor or of Odium, struggling to capture Oathgates and turn the tide of the war in their favor.

Scott White is a freelance contributor to IGN, assisting with tabletop games and guide coverage. Follow him on X/Twitter or Bluesky .

articles.title: GTA 6 Fans Think They Found Jason and Lucia's Vice City Apartment in Real Life
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartment – but don't expect to ever visit it yourself.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 fans think they've spotted the real-life inspiration for Jason and Lucia's Vice City apartment – but don't expect to ever visit it yourself.

Grand Theft Auto players have proven time and time again that they will go to the ends of the earth to learn the smallest details about Rockstar Games experiences, and that hasn't changed for GTA 6. Just days after the big extended look presentation revealed Jason and Lucia's apartment in Vice City, one watcher took it upon themselves to hunt down what appears to be the same apartment in real-life Miami.

Instagram user prettyboycuh was the first to publicly share the location, saying they started by using Google Maps to find a tall teal building that was first shown in last week's gameplay trailer. They said "that was easy," but when they used the Street View function to turn to where Jason and Lucia's apartment should be, all they found was a patch of grass. Then, they turned back the clock.

They – and you can still see this for yourself, too – changed the map's time period from March 2026 to April 2013, around four months before the launch of GTA 5 , and voila, the apartment appeared. Rockstar hasn't officially confirmed what was known as the Belmar Condominium to be the inspiration for the spot we see Jason and Lucia hanging out at in GTA 6, but the similarities are too difficult to ignore. It's the same color, has the same fence, many of the buildings around it are the same, and we can even see the parking lot Jason pulled out of in the extended look. So, where'd it go?

IGN replicated prettyboycuh's findings and can report that the building stuck around through 2017 before it was repainted from its salmon color to some darker grays. It shows up on Google Maps through 2022 before a 2024 recording shows that the Miami location completely vanished.

prettyboycuh took things one step further and found a report from the South Florida Business Journal stating that The Belmar Condo was sold for a total of $12 million in 2022. The same report stated the building was established in 1973 before it was eventually demolished sometime after the buyout. In other words, if you're a GTA 6 fan looking to visit what could become one of the most recognizable locations in Jason and Lucia's story, you're out of luck.

Still, you can see the location through Google Maps to this day, and prettyboycuh discovered that Rockstar inadvertently gave fans more to gawk at, too. Archived Zillow listings show the developer was not only thorough when mapping the outside of the apartment but the inside, too. From the brief glimpses we see of Jason grabbing drinks from the fridge, watching TV, and failing to impress Lucia with his outfit choices, it looks like their apartment pretty closely matches the real-life inspiration.

GTA 6 gave fans about 27 minutes of in-game footage last Thursday, and if this is the length players are going to already, there's no telling what the community will be like when the game actually launches. Previously, fans have (incorrectly) looked to the stars for hints , while others have taken things a bit too far . We'll all be able to revisit Vice City when it launches November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Be sure to also learn about what GTA 6 won't have at launch and the streamer who believes Rockstar designed a character based on himself . IGN recently got to learn a lot about the new Grand Theft Auto, but you can check out just 99 of our favorite details here . Our preview and interview are both also available for those looking to learn more.
